daily_summary.html:
Domestic Politics

President Prabowo led a nationwide military-assisted harvest across 43 locations on Friday, with the TNI's participation aimed at strengthening national food self-sufficiency. The TNI Commander noted that TNI Air Force assistance contributed 45 percent to the 2026 national sugar production target. Separately, the Navy opened 3,110 hectares of new soybean land to support import reduction efforts.

  • PKS inaugurated Rahmat Saleh to lead Gema Keadilan for the 2026-2031 period.
  • Vice President Cak Imin joked about wanting to resign as "captain" after PKB fell behind PKS and Golkar in performance.
  • Deputy Home Affairs Minister Bima Arya urged regional leaders to share best practices in governance during a knowledge-sharing session.
  • A DPR member demanded that the Ministry of Social Affairs evaluate why the Sekolah Rakyat program has attracted few enrollees.
  • The Attorney General's Office appointed North Sumatra chief prosecutor Muhibuddin to a special team investigating the former head of special crimes.
  • Hotman Paris confirmed he is representing former Jampidsus Febrie Adriansyah during questioning at the Attorney General's Office, stating Febrie denies receiving Rp 50 billion from businessman Tan Kian.
  • A DPR member criticized the proposal to reinstate high school tuition fees as a sign of regression in education policy.
  • The discussion on revision of the Election Law continues to be delayed due to two main factors.

Foreign Policy & Defence

Coordinating Minister Airlangga Hartarto said Indonesia is ready to support an open and inclusive AI ecosystem, as the country joined China and others as founding members of a global AI organization. Indonesia reaffirmed its commitment to international technology cooperation and digital innovation. A UI observer commented that Indonesia's position on the ICC aligns with constitutional mandates.

  • Indonesia and Peru expect the IP-CEPA agreement to boost Indonesian exports to Peru to US$745 million, according to a minister.
  • The governor of Nusa Tenggara Barat and Moroccan officials explored cooperation in tourism and renewable energy.
  • Indonesia called on D-8 nations to jointly champion the global climate agenda at COP31.
  • The Indonesian Ambassador stated that Indonesia is ready to lead the development of the global Islamic economy.

Other

President Prabowo announced that Indonesia will stop diesel fuel imports by July 2026 following the successful implementation of the B50 biodiesel program. The President also revealed plans to build up to 50 ethanol plants to support the E20 fuel program and stated that Indonesia will launch a national electric motorcycle. Prabowo also announced a two-year sugarcane rejuvenation program to revitalize the sugar industry.

  • Indonesia launched its first domestically-produced typhoid vaccine, reducing reliance on imports.
  • The Ministry of Villages launched training and certification for 29,830 KDMP managers to improve village economic management.
  • Controversy erupted over the procurement of Rp 1.8 trillion worth of electric fans for Red and White Village Cooperatives.
  • MBG program suppliers threatened a mass strike over unpaid bills, with a fruit vendor reporting Rp 170 million in unpaid melon orders after seven months.
  • The Ombudsman urged prevention of maladministration to strengthen BPJS Kesehatan services.
  • A deputy minister highlighted that storytelling is key to global creative economy success.
